question: What will be Bitcoin's hash rate on December 31, 2026?

calls.reasoning: CMBI hash rate is 1,036,222 PH/s (Oct 30, 2026); the Oct 31 difficulty of 148.36T implies ~1,062 EH/s. In 2026 hashrate fell from the ~1.07-1.12 ZH/s peak to a Q3 average of ~940 EH/s, then recovered in October, with readings from 930 to 1,230 EH/s depending on source. Hashprice back above $40 supports a modest upward drift; the miners' AI/HPC pivot and a projected -3.5% adjustment on Nov 12 push the other way. Median set near the current level (~1.055M), with a ~9% SD covering 2-month drift plus daily index noise. No matching human market: the only Manifold candidate (2^100 hashes/yr before 2035) is a different contract, so it was not used.
calls.dossier:
- CMBI hash rate (resolution source, units PH/s, 48h lookback): 1,036,221.55 PH/s on 2026-10-30; 24h range 995,658-1,058,347; +3.31% day-on-day (indexes.coinmetrics.io/cmbihash, fetched 2026-11-01).
- Difficulty adjustment 2026-10-31 at block 973,728: +5.54% to 148.36T (~1,062 EH/s implied). Reported 7-day hashrate 1,064.8 EH/s vs 1,228.44 the week before. Next adjustment ~Nov 12, projected -3.49% to 143.19T. 2026 so far: 11 up and 11 down out of 22 adjustments (tokenpost, 2026-10-31).
- Coinwarz 2026-11-01: hashrate 1.10 ZH/s, difficulty 148.36T.
- October 2026 readings varied widely by source: 932 EH/s (Oct 13), 1,101 (Oct 15), 1,153 (Oct 20, SoChain), 1,131 (Oct 24), 980.9 (Oct 30) (pickaxe.io news).
- Hashrate Index Q3 2026 heatmap: Q1 avg ~1,066 EH/s, Q2 ~1,004, Q3 ~940 (-6.3% QoQ, -12% below the Dec-2025 peak). BTC fell ~50% from ~$126K (Oct 2025) to the low $60Ks by mid-2026, and hashprice hit record lows (low $30s/PH/day). Some analysts expect hashrate to drift lower until price recovers.
- BeInCrypto/Yahoo (Oct 2026): hashrate peaked ~1,123 EH/s in Oct 2025, bottomed ~850 EH/s in Feb 2026, and recovered to ~1,004 EH/s (8.8% below peak). Public miners' realized hashrate fell 15% in H1 2026; listed miners hold $70B+ in AI/HPC contracts, while private and international operators are filling the gap.
- Hashprice ~$36/PH/day on Oct 25 (-11% month-on-month), then back above $40; October 2026 miner revenue ~$1.12B, the best month since January (shattered.io).
- Status quo: about 1.04-1.06M PH/s now.
- Resolves off CMBI daily 'close' for 2026-12-31 in PH/s, not off difficulty-implied or other trackers. Bounds 750k-1.25M are open both ways.
- Event window: a single day (2026-12-31 close); as of 2026-11-01 about 60 days remain.
- Noise: CMBI daily values move ~3-5% from one day to the next. Late-December winter curtailment (e.g., Texas storms) is a downside candidate; a BTC price rally or new-generation ASIC deployment is an upside candidate.
- Searched without finding: the Dec 31, 2025 CMBI value, the current BTC spot price, and any Polymarket/Kalshi hashrate market.

Hashrate grew ~12% from Sep (934 EH/s) to late Oct with BTC flat near $78k, but hashprice has fallen to ~$33/PH/day (near breakeven) and the next adjustment is projected at -3.5%, so drift over the 60-day horizon looks slightly positive at most. No matching human market found (the Manifold 2^100-hashes-before-2035 contract differs in threshold and deadline).

calls.reasoning: CMBI close 1,036k PH/s on Oct 30 2026; difficulty 148.36T implies ~1,062 EH/s; recent 10-day mean ~1,044k. Hashprice near breakeven (~$33-36/PH/day, BTC ~$78k) and AI/HPC pivots cap growth, offset by Sep-Oct recovery momentum; median ~1.05M. Single-day index noise is large (Oct range 861k-1,129k), and late-December winter curtailment (52-wk low 732k) gives a fat left tail. No human market matches the contract (Manifold 2^100-by-2035 is unrelated).
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts: CMBI 1,036k on Oct 30; difficulty implies ~1,062 EH/s; ±5% daily noise; hashprice near breakeven; a -17% Q4 decline in 2025. No factual conflicts. The disagreements are judgment calls about drift (taken as roughly flat to slightly up), the weight on last year's Q4 decline (limited, because that drop came from a price crash), and the size of the escape tails. The 52-week low of 732k, cited in Run 3, shows a single-day close can approach 750k during curtailment, so I set p_below at 2% and shaded p10 slightly lower. Carried forward the runs' ~235k dispersion and widened it modestly. No web access on this run.
